content.text:
Editors can now edit any document, and all 4 tests pass, including your new `editor can edit` test. But I wouldn't merge it yet: the change also opens a hole for other users.

**What breaks:** while combining the two checks, you dropped the `user.id != null` guard from the owner check. Now a user with no `id` can edit any document that has no `ownerId`, because `undefined === undefined` (and `null === null`) counts as a match:

| Case | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `{role:'viewer'}` (no id) editing `{id:'d2'}` (no owner) | false | **true** |
| `{id:null, role:'viewer'}` editing `{ownerId:null}` | false | **true** |
| `{id:'e', role:'editor'}` editing any doc | false | true ✅ (intended) |

I ran the first case against the original code (stashed your changes, then restored them) and it returned false. So this is new with your change. None of the existing tests cover it, which is why they all still pass.

**Suggested fix** for `src/auth.js:5`:
```js
return PRIVILEGED.includes(user.role) || (user.id != null && doc.ownerId === user.id);
```
And a test to go with it:
```js
test('user without id cannot edit unowned doc', () => assert.ok(!canEdit({ role: 'viewer' }, { id: 'd2' })));
```

I haven't changed anything. Do you want me to apply both?
